PullRequest.Title: Suspend layout measurements for hidden chat pickers
PullRequest.Body:

Part of #339863. **Stacked on #340155**: review and merge that caching foundation first. This PR adds hidden-control suspension rather than changing transcript or grid layout.

## Changes

- Add opt-in, default-enabled suspension to responsive toolbar and picker layout. Hidden controls retain dirty action/content/style changes but do not read geometry or schedule fitting work.
- Add `ChatInputPart.setPickerLayoutEnabled`, separate from whole-widget visibility. Both conditions must permit layout.
- Resume toolbars before synchronously refitting pickers. Compact inputs reuse cached toolbar spacing while suspended and refresh editor width on resume.
- Wire the narrow Sessions `ChatView` visibility bridge to the existing active-session and comparison policy. Share comparison predicates with the existing grid controller rather than duplicating policy; preserve the screen-reader exception.
- Defer comparison-driven resume to a cancellable microtask so its CSS is applied before measuring and before the next paint.
- Document the new control-visibility lifecycle contract. No SessionView/grid arithmetic or transcript changes, new settings, or workbench-to-Sessions imports.

The lower PR's constrained-fitting correction is included through a normal signed merge. No history rewrite or screenshot-baseline acceptance.

The cache layer was independently tested: **85 passing**, with all three new fitting regression cases first failing against the prior SHA-verified fitter. Its [corrected component CI](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37541330053) passed **1,483 renders, zero errors, 73 unchanged blocking fixtures, and 102 Playwright tests**. All five prior picker differences were restored byte-for-byte.

Full hosted platform/screenshot checks are not currently attached to this non-main-base PR. Local tests and the following native runs cover the actual combined source. Dependency/CLA checks pass; the external VS Code PR Check is pending.

## Native dbgjs evidence

Reran actual Code OSS with `@hediet/dbgjs@0.1.0-nightly.34970595271` on the exact final head, isolated profiles and unique ports. The shared OS lock covered the whole smoke lifecycle and entire ABBA batch. Fixtures contained 1/3/6 production panes with eight deterministic Markdown/TypeScript turns each and an unsent first-pane draft.

- Real `BrowserWindow.setBounds` mixed/width-only/height-only resizing and real sash drags.
- Hidden dirty-content diagnostic, repeated twice per revision: **552 monitored geometry/measurement operations to zero**.
- Six-pane mixed diagnostic: **5,720-6,335 hidden geometry reads to zero**. Total intrinsic measurements **768-840 to 3**, clones **768-840 to 6**, presentation writes **1,752-1,932 to 18**. Delivered native resizes were 32-35 before and 42-45 after.
- No matched visible geometry/presentation/ARIA/focus/draft/selection/history mismatches.
- Reactivation agrees synchronously with next-frame state and a fresh exact fit.
- All **39 input-height changes** (33 native, six sash) synchronously updated dependent transcript sizing while typing. Keyboard picker interaction and focus restoration passed.
- Ten disposed picker layouts had zero queued callbacks or pending work.

### Final-stack performance

**Unoptimized baseline to the entire corrected stack**, not an isolated suspension-only speedup. Baseline source equivalence was verified against `d070672f`. Two repetitions per revision in ABBA order, 180 requested updates per case at 16ms spacing. Timings were untraced/unprofiled and separate from dbgjs counters and the diagnostic trace; counter wrappers were removed and the dbgjs target released during timing.

| Panes | Mixed resize: layouts / delivered resize, original to final | p95 rAF gap, original to final |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 16.9-17.1 to 11.2-11.6 | 16.7-16.9 to 16.7 ms |
| 3 | 50.7 to 28.5-28.6 | 41.6-42.1 to 33.3-33.6 ms |
| 6 | 126.3-127.8 to 56.3-56.5 | 91.4-100.2 to 67.6-76.9 ms |

The earlier suspension-only comparison is retained separately in the local evidence and predates the final fitting correction; it is not relabelled as this final run. The final hidden-work diagnostic directly verifies this PR's suspension effect.

Limitations:
- Six panes still exceed a smooth-frame budget; two repetitions show variability, not statistical confidence. More frames/resize events are delivered after the fix, so raw long-task totals need that denominator.
- Native fixtures use deterministic local models without a provider catalogue. Provider icons/configuration/nested-toolbar cases have real-CSS regression and CI fixture coverage; comparison/screen-reader policy has unit coverage, not authenticated native coverage.
- The aggressive correctness smoke had ten ResizeObserver-loop warnings; all four scored matrix lifecycles had none. Development transcript/menu listener-threshold warnings and expected signed-out cloud-provider messages occur in both builds.
- An artificial individual-widget hide/show followed by slot removal had a blank-transcript behavior in both earlier baseline and patched checks; it is outside this picker change.

## Manual checks

1. Open multiple populated Agents panes. Continuously resize the window and sashes with one pane active.
2. Change content/action availability while a pane's controls are inactive, then activate it at a different width. Its latest content and fitting should be correct before interaction.
3. Type a multiline draft during resizing; verify synchronous input/transcript geometry and preserved draft, focus and selection.
4. Exercise comparison input visibility and its existing hide-input setting, including the screen-reader exception.
5. Close panes with work queued and reopen/activate retained panes; no stale callbacks or stale picker state should appear.

All five final native lifecycles completed and cleaned up: five profiles removed, twenty debug ports closed, temporary debugger tooling removed, six final compiled modules restored and hash-verified, and 69 extension output/dependency roots verified worktree-local. No owned app remains.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize the Sessions window or grid with multiple inactive chat panes whose picker controls are hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver delivery and picker/toolbar fitting run before the resized UI settles. The diff gates inactive controls before geometry reads, so hidden panes no longer add fitting work to this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM geometry reads, responsive action fitting, and on cold measurements cloned DOM insertion/removal plus bounds reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, up to two picker layouts and two responsive toolbar relayouts per ChatView could react to resize/content changes; after the diff, inactive non-comparison views perform zero such hidden measurements until one resume.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Hidden controls remained observed and responsive layout continued to read geometry and fit actions on resize or invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These synchronous DOM operations consume resize-frame time; the new gates remove them for hidden controls rather than adding a boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible ChatView count and resize-event frequency; each view owns up to two responsive toolbars and two picker layouts. Measurement-clone work occurs on cold/invalidated picker measurements, while geometry fitting otherwise uses cached thresholds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser observers deliver on the single UI thread. Each picker already coalesces scheduled work to one animation-frame callback, and disabling clears pending callbacks; no parallel subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm picker thresholds remain retained while suspended. Content/style invalidation clears the measurement cache but does not schedule hidden work; the next resume performs one cold measurement. Toolbar minimum-width dirtiness is similarly retained until resume.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the CSS hides inactive controls while the changed active-state bridge disables both toolbar and picker layout, and both layout implementations now check the gate before geometry work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact pane counts and per-layout duration vary with picker content and cache state, but the removed hidden-work mechanism and UI-thread reachability are direct.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate an inactive session or reveal all inputs when entering/completing a comparison grid
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The newly visible controls must refit before interaction/paint. Toolbars resume first, then picker layouts synchronously fit; non-active comparison resumes are deferred to cancellable microtasks so grid CSS is applied first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous toolbar width fitting, picker geometry reads, and potentially cold intrinsic-size clone measurement
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four component resumes per newly shown ChatView, with clone measurement only for invalidated picker lanes; comparison reveal scales with the effective visible-pane count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Picker and toolbar layouts stayed enabled continuously, including while controls were hidden, so no explicit resume pass existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The one-time resume is on the reveal critical path so controls are fit before paint. Before the diff, this work was not a resume cost because layouts remained active and repeatedly paid while hidden; the change bounds it to visibility transitions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session for normal activation, or all visible comparison panes when comparison policy reveals inactive inputs; each resumed view has at most two toolbars and two picker layouts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resume work is serialized on the UI thread. Comparison-driven enables use one cancellable microtask per affected ChatView; repeated state changes cancel stale microtasks through the autorun reader store.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A width-only resume reuses warm picker thresholds. Hidden content/theme/config changes invalidate thresholds and cause one cold clone-based measurement on resume; toolbar action changes leave one dirty minimum-width recomputation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call order, synchronous enable behavior, cache checks, and cancellable microtask are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact one-time resume latency depends on DOM size and whether caches were invalidated, but it replaces repeated hidden work and is bounded by visible panes.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional bounded scheduling tradeoff with coalescing/cancellation; no actionable regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change picker actions, labels, themes, or configuration while controls are hidden, then reveal them
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Action DOM updates still occur when their authoritative menus change, but responsive geometry and fitting are deferred off the hidden critical path and consolidated into the first resume.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DOM action rendering followed by deferred intrinsic-size and geometry measurement on resume
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Potentially many hidden mutations, but at most one responsive recomputation per toolbar/picker lane when re-enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each hidden invalidation could schedule layout on the next animation frame and perform geometry work despite invisibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Measurement is off the hidden-update path and paid once on reveal; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of hidden picker lanes and action/content changes during the hidden lifetime; effective fitting cardinality is one per lane at resume rather than one per change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutation and resize notifications remain browser-driven on the UI thread. The disabled state prevents frame scheduling, and a single synchronous resume consumes the accumulated dirty state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Content/style changes invalidate picker measurements; repeated invalidations collapse into the same empty-cache state. Toolbar action replacement sets one dirty flag. Width-only changes preserve picker thresholds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: disabled scheduling, retained dirty flags, invalidation semantics, and synchronous resume are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Menu churn frequency varies, but dirty-state coalescing and the lack of hidden geometry work are directly established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update active session/comparison/configuration state across several ChatView instances
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each ChatView autorun scans visible sessions and comparisons to decide whether its picker layout is enabled. The scan is synchronous but runs only on active/comparison/visibility-policy changes, not resize, typing, rendering, or scrolling.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible ChatView count multiplied by comparison and participant counts; effective product usage has a small visible-pane set, and the trigger is infrequent state change rather than a frame-level event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All scans are synchronous on one UI thread; resulting comparison resumes are cancellable microtasks and do not cross process boundaries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observable dependencies suppress runs when unrelated state is unchanged. There is no result cache, but scans are tied to low-frequency policy changes; picker measurement caches remain independent.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added repeated scan, low for material performance impact because triggers are infrequent and visible-pane cardinality is limited.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository code does not impose a tiny comparison-history bound, but no realistic hot trigger or expensive boundary was found that would make these URI comparisons a reportable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: Diff adds modest repeated CPU bookkeeping but no concrete user-visible performance regression under a realistic trigger.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and traced hidden resize/layout, resume, invalidation, comparison-policy, cache, scheduling, and disposal paths. The change removes repeated hidden DOM measurement, preserves dirty cache state, cancels stale work, and introduces only bounded one-time resume/layout work. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.
